labelInUi: Prepared output — read the mode field before describing this on stage

modeContract.attested: actions/attest-build-provenance ran and GitHub issued a signed attestation. The attestation URL is real and verifiable with gh attestation verify.
modeContract.simulated: The attestation step did not run or was not entitled. The record below describes the shape of a provenance statement and proves nothing about this artefact.
modeContract.rule: Never describe a simulated record as a verified one. scripts/verify.mjs reads the mode field and prints it.

record.reason: Captured on a repository without an attestation entitlement at capture time.
record.subject: out/bundle/showcase-bundle.tar.gz
wouldProve: Which workflow file built the artefact
Which commit SHA it was built from
Which runner and which run id produced it
That the artefact was not altered after the build

environmentApproval.control: A GitHub environment holds required reviewers and the deployment secrets. A job targeting it waits for a named human before it runs.
environmentApproval.whyItMatters: The approval is on the deployment, not on the merge. Merging is a code decision; deploying is an authority decision, and they are separable.

oidc.control: The deployment job requests a short-lived OIDC token with id-token: write and exchanges it with the cloud provider. No long-lived cloud credential is stored in the repository.
oidc.whyItMatters: The trust relationship names a repository, a branch or an environment. Widen it and you widen the blast radius; that is a reviewable line in a Terraform file, not a hidden setting.

releasePattern.terraform: The deployment job runs plan on the pull request and apply after the environment approval. The plan is the reviewable proposal; the apply is the authorised act.
releasePattern.kubernetes: The same shape with a manifest or a chart: render and diff on the pull request, apply after approval, and let the cluster's admission policy reject anything the pipeline did not sign.
releasePattern.commonProperty: In both cases the agent may propose. It may not apply.

verifiableClaims: The workflow declares id-token: write and attestations: write only on the job that needs them.
Every third-party action in the release workflow is pinned to a full commit SHA.
The provenance record states its own mode, so a simulation cannot be mistaken for a verified attestation.
